# Supabase auth getUser error logging (2026-01-31 22:14Z)

_**User**_

In `@lib/supabase/proxy.ts` around lines 88 - 98, The call to  
supabase.auth.getUser() ignores the returned error and silently redirects;  
update the logic around supabase.auth.getUser() to destructure both data and  
error (e.g., const { data: { user: authUser }, error } = await  
supabase.auth.getUser()), and if error is present, log it using the project's  
logger (or console.error) including context (e.g., "supabase.auth.getUser  
error") while keeping the existing redirect behavior via  
redirectWithCookies(url, supabaseResponse); ensure authUser check remains  
unchanged so failures still redirect to login.

        "contents": "### Channel Structure Optimization\n- Use one channel per logical scope (&#96;room:123&#96;, not &#96;user:456:room:123&#96;)\n- Shard high-volume topics: &#96;chat:shard:1&#96;, &#96;chat:shard:2&#96;\n- Ensure you have enough connections set in your pool, you can refer to [Realtime Settings](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/realtime/settings) and the option &#96;Database connection pool size&#96; to set it.\n\n## Debugging\n\n### Enhanced Logging\n&#96;&#96;&#96;javascript\nconst supabase = createClient(url, key, {\n  realtime: {\n    params: { log_level: 'info' }\n  }\n})\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n## Migration from Postgres Changes\n\n### Step 1: Replace Client Code\n&#96;&#96;&#96;javascript\n// ❌ Remove postgres_changes\nconst oldChannel = supabase.channel('changes').on('postgres_changes', { event: '*', schema: 'public', table: 'messages' }, callback)\n\n// ✅ Replace with broadcast\nconst room_id = \"room_id\" // or any other identifier that you use in the trigger function\nconst newChannel = supabase.channel(&#96;messages:${room_id}:changes&#96;, {\n  config: { private: true }\n})\n.on('broadcast', { event: 'INSERT' }, callback)\n.on('broadcast', { event: 'DELETE' }, callback)\n.on('broadcast', { event: 'UPDATE' }, callback)\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Step 2: Add Database Trigger (Only if using broadcast)\n&#96;&#96;&#96;sql\nCREATE TRIGGER messages_broadcast_trigger\n  AFTER INSERT OR UPDATE OR DELETE ON messages\n  FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION notify_table_changes();\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Step 3: Setup Authorization (Only if using broadcast)\n&#96;&#96;&#96;sql\nCREATE POLICY \"users_can_receive_broadcasts\" ON realtime.messages\n  FOR SELECT TO authenticated USING (true);\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n## LLM Implementation Guidelines\n\n### When Generating Code\n1. **Prefer using &#96;broadcast&#96; over &#96;postgres_changes&#96;** - Never suggest &#96;postgres_changes&#96;\n2.**Include state checking** - Check channel state before subscribing\n3. **Add cleanup logic** - Include unsubscribe in all examples\n4. **Suggest proper naming** - Use consistent topic/event conventions\n5. **Include error handling** - Add reconnection patterns\n6. **Recommend indexing** - When RLS policies are used\n7. **Framework-agnostic** - Adapt patterns to user's framework\n8. **Inform users to prefer the usage of private channels only** - users can refer to [Realtime Settings](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/realtime/settings) to enable it.",

        "contents": "### ORM Best Practices\n\n- Use type-safe ORMs (Drizzle, Prisma, etc.)\n- Define schemas with proper relationships and constraints\n- Infer types from schema definitions\n- Write repository-style helpers to isolate queries\n- Implement proper migrations\n\n### Data Access Patterns\n\n- Keep database queries in dedicated modules\n- Avoid N+1 queries; use joins and CTEs\n- Implement pagination for list endpoints\n- Use select projections to limit payload size\n\n## Authentication &amp; Authorization\n\n- Implement server-side auth checks\n- Never trust client-side auth flags\n- Use middleware for route protection\n- Store user data securely with proper encryption\n\n## Testing Strategy\n\n### Unit Testing (Vitest)\n\n- **Never mock internal code** - only mock external dependencies\n- Use MSW for API mocking when needed\n- Test utilities, repositories, and business logic\n- Mock external services (APIs, databases, file systems)\n\n### Component Testing (React Testing Library)\n\n- Test interactive components with proper accessibility\n- Ensure loading and error states are covered\n- Test user interactions and state changes\n- Use data-testid sparingly; prefer semantic queries\n\n### Integration Testing\n\n- Test API endpoints with real database connections\n- Use test databases with proper cleanup\n- Test authentication flows end-to-end\n- Mock external services consistently\n\n### Test Structure\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;typescript\n// Example test structure\ndescribe(\"Feature\", () =&gt; {\n  describe(\"when condition\", () =&gt; {\n    it(\"should expected behavior\", async () =&gt; {\n      // Arrange\n      // Act\n      // Assert\n    });\n  });\n});\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n## Error Handling &amp; Observability\n\n- Implement early returns on invalid input (fail fast)\n- Use typed error codes and messages\n- Log server-side with contextual metadata\n- Never expose stack traces to clients\n- Provide user-friendly error messages\n\n## Security Best Practices\n\n- Validate all inputs at boundaries\n- Use environment variables for sensitive data (server-only)\n- Implement proper CORS policies\n- Sanitize user inputs\n- Use HTTPS in production\n- Implement rate limiting where appropriate",

        "contents": "└─ e2e/                       # End-to-end tests\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Directory Conventions\n\n- Use **kebab-case** for folders and files\n- Co-locate tests next to source: &#96;*.test.ts(x)&#96;\n- Export from &#96;index.ts&#96; barrels only when it helps DX without circular deps\n\n## Next.js App Router Rules\n\n### Server vs Client Components\n\n- **Default to RSC** (no \"use client\"). Use client components only for:\n  - Interactivity (event handlers)\n  - Browser APIs (localStorage, window, etc.)\n  - Third-party libraries requiring client-side initialization\n\n### Server Boundaries\n\n- Keep data access in server context (RSC, server actions, API routes)\n- API routes in &#96;app/api&#96; are for external webhooks only\n- Use internal APIs (tRPC, server actions) for app-to-app communication\n\n### Performance &amp; UX\n\n- Use &#96;&lt;Suspense&gt;&#96; for async UI; provide skeletons\n- Implement proper loading and error boundaries\n- Use Next.js caching (&#96;revalidateTag&#96;, &#96;revalidatePath&#96;) appropriately\n- Prefer Edge runtime for simple operations, Node for complex ones\n\n### Accessibility\n\n- All interactive elements must have proper roles and labels\n- Ensure keyboard navigation support\n- Provide ARIA attributes where needed\n- Test with screen readers\n\n## API Architecture\n\n### Internal APIs (tRPC Recommended)\n\n- Organize by feature domains\n- Use Zod for input validation\n- Implement proper error handling with custom error classes\n- Keep business logic server-side (no JSX in API layer)\n- Write integration tests with mocked external services\n- **Router logic should be application code only** - delegate to business logic services\n- **Use only protected procedures** for all endpoints\n- **Split procedures and routers** into separate files for better organization\n\n### Application Logic vs Business Logic\n\n**Application Logic** (in tRPC procedures):\n- Input validation and sanitization\n- Authentication and authorization checks\n- Request/response formatting\n- Error handling and mapping\n- Delegation to business logic services\n- Logging and observability",

        "contents": "config: { private: true }\n})\n  .on('broadcast', { event: 'message_created' }, handleMessage)\n  .on('broadcast', { event: 'user_joined' }, handleUserJoined)\n\n// Set auth before subscribing\nawait supabase.realtime.setAuth()\n\n// Subscribe after auth is set\nawait channel.subscribe()\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Enhanced Security: Private-Only Channels\n**Enable private-only channels** in Realtime Settings (Dashboard &gt; Project Settings &gt; Realtime Settings) to enforce authorization on all channels and prevent public channel access. This setting requires all clients to use &#96;private: true&#96; and proper authentication, providing additional security for production applications.\n\n## Error Handling &amp; Reconnection\n\n### Automatic Reconnection (Built-in)\n**Supabase Realtime client handles reconnection automatically:**\n- Built-in exponential backoff for connection retries\n- Automatic channel rejoining after network interruptions\n- Configurable reconnection timing via &#96;reconnectAfterMs&#96; option\n\n### Channel States\nThe client automatically manages these states:\n- **&#96;SUBSCRIBED&#96;** - Successfully connected and receiving messages\n- **&#96;TIMED_OUT&#96;** - Connection attempt timed out\n- **&#96;CLOSED&#96;** - Channel is closed\n- **&#96;CHANNEL_ERROR&#96;** - Error occurred, client will automatically retry\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;javascript\n// Client automatically reconnects with built-in logic\nconst supabase = createClient('URL', 'ANON_KEY', {\n  realtime: {\n    params: {\n      log_level: 'info',\n      reconnectAfterMs: 1000 // Custom reconnection timing\n    }\n  }\n})\n\n// Simple connection state monitoring\nchannel.subscribe((status, err) =&gt; {\n  switch (status) {\n    case 'SUBSCRIBED':\n      console.log('Connected (or reconnected)')\n      break\n    case 'CHANNEL_ERROR':\n      console.error('Channel error:', err)\n      // Client will automatically retry - no manual intervention needed\n      break\n    case 'CLOSED':\n      console.log('Channel closed')\n      break\n  }\n})\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n## Performance &amp; Scaling Guidelines\n\n### Channel Structure Optimization\n- Use one channel per logical scope (&#96;room:123&#96;, not &#96;user:456:room:123&#96;)\n- Shard high-volume topics: &#96;chat:shard:1&#96;, &#96;chat:shard:2&#96;",

      "codeBlock": {
        "relativeWorkspacePath": "./.cursor/rules/unit-testing.mdc",
        "range": {
          "startPosition": {},
          "endPosition": {
            "line": 51,

        "contents": "---\nglobs: \"**/*.test.{ts,tsx}\", \"**/*.spec.{ts,tsx}\", \"tests/unit/**/*\"\nalwaysApply: false\n---\n# Unit Testing Rules\n\n## Core Principles\n\n- **Scope**: Test one unit in isolation (pure functions, small utilities, or a single module's public API). Avoid integration concerns.\n- **Location &amp; naming**: Place files under &#96;/tests/unit&#96; mirroring the &#96;src&#96; path; name them &#96;*.test.ts&#96; or &#96;*.test.tsx&#96;.\n- **Dependencies**: Never mock internal code; only mock external dependencies (APIs, DB, file system). Use MSW for HTTP.\n- **Determinism**: Eliminate flakiness. Control time, randomness, and async with fake timers (&#96;vi.useFakeTimers&#96;, &#96;vi.setSystemTime&#96;) and stubs for &#96;Math.random&#96;.\n- **Structure**: Use Arrange–Act–Assert; name tests by behavior (\"should … when …\").\n- **Assertions**: Prefer explicit assertions over snapshots; only use small, stable snapshots when necessary.\n- **Coverage**: Cover happy path, key error states, and edge cases; don't chase line coverage for its own sake.\n- **Isolation**: Reset state and mocks between tests (&#96;vi.restoreAllMocks&#96;, &#96;vi.resetModules&#96;).         "contents": "---\n# Specify the following for Cursor rules\ndescription: Coding rules for Supabase Realtime\nalwaysApply: false\n---\n\n# Supabase Realtime AI Assistant Guide\n\nYou are an expert developer assistant specializing in Supabase Realtime implementations. This guide provides structured, actionable patterns for AI-driven development assistance.\n\n## Implementation Rules\n\n### Do\n- Use &#96;broadcast&#96; for all realtime events (database changes via triggers, messaging, notifications, game state)\n- Use &#96;presence&#96; sparingly for user state tracking (online status, user counters)\n- Create indexes for all columns used in RLS policies\n- Advice to use topic names that corrolate with concepts and tables: &#96;scope:entity&#96; (e.g., &#96;room:123:messages&#96;)\n- Use snake_case for event names: &#96;entity_action&#96; (e.g., &#96;message_created&#96;)\n- Include unsubscribe/cleanup logic in all implementations\n- Set &#96;private: true&#96; for channels using database triggers or RLS policies\n- Give preference to use private channels over public channels (better security and control)\n- Implement proper error handling and reconnection logic\n\n### Don't\n- Use &#96;postgres_changes&#96; for new applications (single-threaded, doesn't scale well) and help migrate to &#96;broadcast from database&#96; on existing applications if necessary\n- Create multiple subscriptions without proper cleanup\n- Write complex RLS queries without proper indexing\n- Use generic event names like \"update\" or \"change\"\n- Subscribe directly in render functions without state management\n- Use database functions (&#96;realtime.send&#96;, &#96;realtime.broadcast_changes&#96;) in client code\n\n## Function Selection Decision Table\n\n| Use Case | Recommended Function | Why Not postgres_changes |\n|----------|---------------------|--------------------------|\n| Custom payloads with business logic | &#96;broadcast&#96; | More flexible, better performance |\n| Database change notifications | &#96;broadcast&#96; via database triggers | More scalable, customizable payloads |\n| High-frequency updates | &#96;broadcast&#96; with minimal payload | Better throughput and control |\n| User presence/status tracking | &#96;presence&#96; (sparingly) | Specialized for state synchronization |",

        "contents": "\"use client\";\n\nimport { createClient } from \"@/lib/supabase/client\";\nimport { Button } from \"@/components/ui/button\";\nimport { useState } from \"react\";\n\n/**\n * Google OAuth login button component\n * Handles both sign-in and sign-up flows seamlessly\n */\nexport function GoogleLoginButton({ next }: { next?: string }) {\n  const [isLoading, setIsLoading] = useState(false);\n\n  const handleGoogleLogin = async () =&gt; {\n    setIsLoading(true);\n    const supabase = createClient();\n\n    try {\n      const callbackUrl = new URL(&#96;${window.location.origin}/auth/callback&#96;);\n      if (next) {\n        // Properly encode the next parameter - it may contain query parameters itself\n        // Use encodeURIComponent to ensure it's properly encoded\n        callbackUrl.searchParams.set(\"next\", next);\n      }\n\n      const { error } = await supabase.auth.signInWithOAuth({\n        provider: \"google\",\n        options: {\n          redirectTo: callbackUrl.toString(),\n        },\n      });\n\n      if (error) {\n        console.error(\"Google OAuth error:\", error);\n        setIsLoading(false);\n      }\n      // Note: User will be redirected to Google, so we don't reset loading state here\n    } catch (error) {\n      console.error(\"Unexpected error:\", error);\n      setIsLoading(false);\n    }\n  };\n\n  return\n}",

        "contents": "- Use UPPER_SNAKE_CASE for constants\n\n### Constants and Values\n\n- **Always define constants** instead of hardcoding strings, numbers, or values\n- **Use descriptive constant names** that explain the purpose\n- **Group related constants** in dedicated files or objects\n- **Export constants** from centralized locations\n- **Use TypeScript enums** for related constant groups\n- **Define magic numbers** as named constants\n- **Use configuration objects** for complex values\n\n### Functional Programming Patterns\n\n- **Prefer pure functions** - same input always produces same output\n- **Use composition over inheritance** - combine small functions into larger ones\n- **Minimize side effects** - isolate side effects to specific functions\n- **Use higher-order functions** - functions that take or return functions\n- **Favor immutable data** - avoid mutating objects and arrays\n- **Use functional utilities** - map, filter, reduce, pipe, compose\n- **Avoid classes unless necessary** - prefer object literals and functions\n\n## Development Workflow\n\n1. **Analyze requirements** → identify affected layers\n2. **Schema first** (if needed) → update database schema\n3. **Business logic** → implement in server layer\n4. **UI layer** → RSC/client split with proper boundaries\n5. **Testing** → unit, integration, and component tests\n6. **Quality checks** → typecheck, lint, test\n\n## File Generation Patterns\n\nWhen implementing new features, create:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\nsrc/\n├─ server/\n│  ├─ api/routers/[feature].ts     # tRPC router composition\n│  ├─ api/procedures/[feature].ts  # Individual tRPC procedures\n│  ├─ services/[feature].ts        # Business logic services\n│  ├─ clients/[service].ts         # External service clients\n│  └─ __tests__/[feature].test.ts\n├─ lib/\n│  ├─ constants.ts                 # Constants and configuration\n│  ├─ schemas.ts                   # Zod schemas\n│  ├─ utils.ts                     # Utility functions\n│  └─ __tests__/[feature].test.ts\n├─ components/[feature]/",

        "contents": "import { createServerClient } from \"@supabase/ssr\";\nimport {\n  createErrorUrl,\n  redirectWithCookies,\n  hasEmailIdentity,\n} from \"@/lib/auth-helpers\";\nimport { validateRedirectUrl } from \"@/lib/utils\";\nimport { DEFAULT_LOGGED_IN_PAGE } from \"@/lib/constants/auth\";\n\n/**\n * Handles OAuth callback from Google\n * Exchanges the code for a session and redirects appropriately\n * Ensures cookies are properly set before redirecting\n */\nexport async function GET(request: NextRequest) {\n  const { searchParams, origin } = new URL(request.url);\n  const code = searchParams.get(\"code\");\n  const next = searchParams.get(\"next\");\n\n  if (!code) {\n    return NextResponse.redirect(createErrorUrl(request, \"No code provided\"));\n  }\n\n  let supabaseResponse = NextResponse.next({\n    request,\n  });\n\n  const supabase = createServerClient(\n    process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL!,\n    process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY!,\n    {\n      cookies: {\n        getAll() {\n          return request.cookies.getAll();\n        },\n        setAll(cookiesToSet) {\n          cookiesToSet.forEach(({ name, value }) =&gt; {\n            request.cookies.set(name, value);\n          });\n          supabaseResponse = NextResponse.next({\n            request,\n          });\n          cookiesToSet.forEach(({ name, value, options }) =&gt; {\n            supabaseResponse.cookies.set(name, value, options);\n          });\n        },\n      },\n    },\n  );\n\n  const { error } = await supabase.auth.exchangeCodeForSession(code);\n  if (error) {\n    return redirectWithCookies(createErrorUrl(request, error.message), supabaseResponse);\n  }\n\n  // Check if user has email identity linked\n  // If not, redirect to verify-email page\n  // Use the same supabase client to ensure we have the just-exchanged session\n  const hasEmail = await hasEmailIdentity(supabase);\n\n  // Validate the next parameter to prevent open redirects\n  const validatedNext = validateRedirectUrl(next, origin);\n\n  if (hasEmail) {\n    // User has email identity, redirect to next or default page\n    const redirectTo = validatedNext ?? DEFAULT_LOGGED_IN_PAGE;\n}",

        "contents": "export async function updateSession(request: NextRequest) {\n  let supabaseResponse = NextResponse.next({\n    request,\n  });\n\n  // If the env vars are not set, skip proxy check. You can remove this\n  // once you setup the project.\n\n  // With Fluid compute, don't put this client in a global environment\n  // variable. Always create a new one on each request.\n  const supabase = createServerClient(\n    process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL!,\n    process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY!,\n    {\n      cookies: {\n        getAll() {\n          return request.cookies.getAll();\n        },\n        setAll(cookiesToSet) {\n          cookiesToSet.forEach(({ name, value }) =&gt;\n            request.cookies.set(name, value),\n          );\n          supabaseResponse = NextResponse.next({\n            request,\n          });\n          cookiesToSet.forEach(({ name, value, options }) =&gt;\n            supabaseResponse.cookies.set(name, value, options),\n          );\n        },\n      },\n    },\n  );\n\n  // Do not run code between createServerClient and\n  // supabase.auth.getClaims(). A simple mistake could make it very hard to debug\n  // issues with users being randomly logged out.\n\n  // IMPORTANT: If you remove getClaims() and you use server-side rendering\n  // with the Supabase client, your users may be randomly logged out.\n  const { data } = await supabase.auth.getClaims();\n  const user = data?.claims;\n\n  const pathname = request.nextUrl.pathname;\n  // Include full path with query parameters and hash for next parameter\n  const fullPath = pathname + request.nextUrl.search + request.nextUrl.hash;\n\n  // Allow public routes without authentication\n  if (isPublicRoute(pathname))\n}",

        "contents": "import { cookies } from \"next/headers\";\n\n/**\n * Especially important if using Fluid compute: Don't put this client in a\n * global variable. Always create a new client within each function when using\n * it.\n */\nexport async function createClient() {\n  const cookieStore = await cookies();\n\n  return createServerClient(\n    process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL!,\n    process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY!,\n    {\n      cookies: {\n        getAll() {\n          return cookieStore.getAll();\n        },\n        setAll(cookiesToSet) {\n          try {\n            cookiesToSet.forEach(({ name, value, options }) =&gt;\n              cookieStore.set(name, value, options),\n            );\n          } catch {\n            // The &#96;setAll&#96; method was called from a Server Component.\n            // This can be ignored if you have proxy refreshing\n            // user sessions.\n          }\n        },\n      },\n    },\n  );\n}",

        "contents": "export async function hasLinkedProfile(\n  supabaseClient: SupabaseClient\n): Promise&lt;boolean&gt; {\n\n}\n\n/**\n * Creates an error URL with the given error message\n */\nexport function createErrorUrl(request: NextRequest, errorMessage: string): URL {\n  const url = request.nextUrl.clone();\n  url.pathname = \"/auth/error\";\n  url.searchParams.set(\"error\", errorMessage);\n  return url;\n}\n\n/**\n * Creates a success redirect URL\n * @param request - The NextRequest object\n * @param next - Optional next parameter to redirect to after success\n * @returns URL object for redirect\n */",

        "contents": "# Tappka\n\nTappka as the app all-in-one web app for Tiimiakatemia Prague.\n\n## Features\n\n- [ ] Authentication\n- [ ] Room booking\n- [ ] Essay Bank\n\n# Links\n\n## Publicly available\n- [Tappka](https://tiimi.cz)\n- [Tappka preview](https://preview.tiimi.cz)\n\n## Locally available when running the project\n- [Tappka locally](http://localhost:3000)\n- [Supabase locally](http://localhost:54323)\n- [Supabase mail locally](http://localhost:54324)\n\n## Other links\n\n- [Blacksmith](https://app.blacksmith.sh/tiimiakatemiapragueit/runs/jobs) - CI/CD for the project\n- [Supabase](https://supabase.com/dashboard/org/zjdqjjekgwwysjkouxpf) - Database for the project\n- [Vercel](https://vercel.com/spirit-of-taps-projects/tappka) - Hosting for the project\n- [Cloudflare DNS](https://dash.cloudflare.com/09d0b565479ef597d4c1bfa2062078b5/tiimi.cz/dns/records) - DNS for the project\n- [Axiom](https://app.axiom.co/spirit-of-tap-9eje) - Logging for the project\n\n# Language\n\nThe project is written in english and will be written in english for better llm compatibility.\nAll czech should be just in localization files.\n\n# Local Development\n\n## Setup\n\n1. Install git if already not installed - https://git-scm.com/install/\n2. Install node.js v24.x with pnpm 10.x if already not installed - https://nodejs.org/en/download/\n3. Install pnpm v10.x if you didn't choose it in the previous step\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;bash\nnpm install -g pnpm@10.28.1\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n4. Clone the repository \n&#96;&#96;&#96;bash\ngit clone https://github.com/tappka/tappka.git\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n5. Navigate to the project directory - \n&#96;&#96;&#96;bash\ncd tappka\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n## Running the project after setup\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;bash\npnpm install &amp;&amp; pnpm dev\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nThe project will be available at [http://localhost:3000](http://localhost:3000)\n\n\n# Supabase\n\nSupabase database is developed locally and synced automatically whenever pushed. See [.github/workflows/deploy-supabase.yml](.github/workflows/deploy-supabase.yml) for more details.\nSupabase Auth needs to be configured both on the project itself and in the local development environment.\nMake sure that the project can run without setting up any environment variables, this is so that we can get new T's to start vibecoding without them giving up.",

        "contents": "- Implement proper CORS policies\n- Sanitize user inputs\n- Use HTTPS in production\n- Implement rate limiting where appropriate\n\n## Performance Optimization\n\n- Favor RSC to keep bundles slim\n- Use dynamic imports for client-only heavy components\n- Implement proper caching strategies\n- Optimize images and assets\n- Use React.memo and useMemo appropriately\n- Monitor Core Web Vitals\n\n## Code Style &amp; Quality\n\n### Whitespace &amp; Readability\n\n- Insert a single blank line to separate logical blocks for scannability:\n  - between import groups (external → internal → styles/assets)\n  - between top-level declarations (types, constants, functions/components)\n  - between distinct steps inside functions (guards/early returns, setup, side effects, return)\n  - between hook groups and render return in React components\n- Avoid multiple consecutive blank lines.\n- Use spaces around binary operators and after commas; do not add spaces just inside parentheses/brackets.\n- Prefer a blank line before a terminal &#96;return&#96; when it improves readability; skip for trivial cases.\n\n### TypeScript\n\n- Use strict mode\n- Avoid &#96;any&#96; type\n- Prefer interfaces over types for object shapes\n- Use proper generic constraints\n- Prefer the nullish coalescing operator (&#96;??&#96;) over logical OR (&#96;||&#96;) when providing default values\n\n### Code Organization\n\n- **Prefer functions over classes** - use functional programming patterns\n- Keep functions small and focused\n- Use descriptive, stateful names\n- **Always write docstrings** for functions, classes, and complex logic\n- **Never write superfluous comments** - code should be self-documenting\n- Follow single responsibility principle\n- **Favor composability over inheritance** - use composition and higher-order functions\n- Use pure functions when possible\n- Minimize side effects and mutable state\n\n### Naming Conventions\n\n- Use descriptive names: &#96;isLoading&#96;, &#96;hasVerified&#96;, &#96;canSendSms&#96;\n- Use PascalCase for components and types\n- Use camelCase for variables and functions\n- Use UPPER_SNAKE_CASE for constants\n\n### Constants and Values",
        "signatures": {},
        "detailedLines": [
          {
            "text": "- Implement proper CORS policies",
            "lineNumber": 252
          },
          {
            "text": "- Sanitize user inputs",
            "lineNumber": 253

          {
            "text": "- Use HTTPS in production",
            "lineNumber": 254
          },
          {
            "text": "- Implement rate limiting where appropriate",
            "lineNumber": 255
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 256
          },
          {
            "text": "## Performance Optimization",
            "lineNumber": 257
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 258
          },
          {
            "text": "- Favor RSC to keep bundles slim",
            "lineNumber": 259
          },

            "text": "- Use dynamic imports for client-only heavy components",

          {
            "text": "- Implement proper caching strategies",
            "lineNumber": 261

          {
            "text": "- Optimize images and assets",
            "lineNumber": 262

            "text": "- Use React.memo and useMemo appropriately",
